title: Fjord Stopwatch (lo-fi beat for late reading)
brief: A lo-fi hip-hop beat for reading late at night, about two and a half minutes, looping without a seam: a worn upright piano over jazzy seventh chords, a round upright bass, a laid-back swung drum kit and a little tape and vinyl character. Four or five parts; one simple melodic idea that keeps coming back.

sections.intent: Kettle: keys, bass and soft drums with the vinyl; the full kit on bar 5
Pulley: cold B harmony, the 3+3+2 kick; no lead
Stopwatch: the hook on the flute with the full hat groove
Wagon: half-time wheels and the cold hook; the piano thins; a fill at the end
Balloon: the hook an octave up; two bars without drums
Patio: the hook home and a question that leads back to bar 0

tracks.name: Upright bass, round and laid back
Drum kit, side stick and closed hats, worn

association.whole: A late reader on a plywood floor over a fjord-side harbour. A pulley outside lifts a wagon of nets; the stopwatch on the sill times a kettle that simmers. A red balloon, lost from the harbour fair, drifts past the patio door and its string brushes the canvas awning; nettles grow through the paving and ooze from an old paint tin in the gutter. The reader rests a cheek on one hand while the balloon rises and comes down again and the night goes on.

gives.what: six scenes of eight bars in the order of the night: kettle, pulley, stopwatch, wagon, balloon, patio
the pulley creaks in 3+3+2 eighths (kick on steps 0, 6, 12) in the pulley and wagon scenes; the stopwatch ticks evenly on the hats
the balloon: a fourth up from C5 to F5, then down by step to A4, the hook; the wagon plays the same shape over the cold chords
the cold fjord turn: D-flat major seventh and the B-flat minor and E-flat seventh colour in the pulley and wagon scenes; the balloon climbs down a circle of fifths
wood and canvas: a side stick, a worn upright piano, an upright bass and a flute for the balloon
the canvas muffles the top: piano low-passed at 5.2 kHz, tape wobble on the piano and flute, vinyl hiss under the whole piece

plan.identity: a two-bar hook for the flute that floats up a fourth and falls back by step, over a piano that answers with rootless sevenths; the B scenes turn cold by a half step.

high_point.means: the hook an octave up on the flute, after two bars with the drums out

sections.differs: no lead; soft hats and a side stick from the first bar, the full kit on bar 5
the 3+3+2 kick, the full kit and the cold harmony; still no lead
the flute enters with the hook and the full hat groove
half-time drums and quarter hats, the cold hook, the piano thins to two hits a bar, a fill
the flute an octave up; two bars with no drums before the answer
the hook back in its home register, then a question on bar 47 that leads back to the first bar

decisions: Tempo 78 BPM, 48 bars (2:28 at this tempo), home key F major; the B scenes borrow D-flat and B-flat minor colours from the words (fjord, the cold turn).

Upright piano (vcsl_keys 0:3, Upright Yamaha) comps rootless voicings on each hit, voiced against the bass and flute so that no minor second or ninth sounds under them (round 2); pedal once a bar, low-passed at 5.2 kHz, given tape wobble; the drum bus ducks it on the kick (2.5 dB).
Upright bass (bass_sneaky 0:32): roots, fifths, an octave, and a chromatic approach into the next chord; it sits on the rhythm of the piece, not a copy of the kick.

Drum kit rusty as one melodic bank (bank 0, program 0: a single kit), side stick on 2 and 4, closed hats with ghost hats on the off-sixteenths, swing 0.58 on sixteenths (the words stopwatch and kettle), a 12-bit bitcrush and saturation as the SP-1200 grit.
Flute (vsco 0:73), legato with a 5-semitone window; each hook is one line of connected notes.
Vinyl: one noise note across the piece, peak-leveled at -30 dBFS.
Loop from bar 0: the drums are on from the first bar (soft); bar 47 is the F-major question that the first bar answers; no fade at either end.

loop_seam.timbre: the flute ends its question on bar 47 and rests through the loop's first bar; it returns on bar 16 with the hook. The piano, bass, drums and vinyl carry the join, and the flute's silence over bars 0-15 is the kettle scene by design. Kept on purpose.

plan:balloon: the balloon keeps the wagon's loudness (its mean written velocity is within three counts of the wagon's). Its height comes from the register, the octave up, and from the two bars without drums; the plan now says so, where it first said softer.
